_about: Source of truth for every translatable UI string (Docs/LOCALIZATION.md). key = the English text exactly as the game shows it (UXML text, C# literal or Credits.txt line). 'where' and 'note' are for translators, 'max' is a soft length limit in characters for Latin/Cyrillic/Greek scripts (CJK: about half). After editing run: python Tools/loc/loc_tool.py sync && python Tools/loc/loc_tool.py check

strings.where: Caption above the left tool strip (the tools that work on the carpet).
strings.note: Uppercase caption.

strings.where: Caption above the right tool strip (the tools for the tiled floor around the carpet).
strings.note: Uppercase caption.

strings.where: Top-right button that opens the upgrade shop (hotkey U, shown on a key chip next to it).
strings.note: Must be the same word as in '{0}: buy it in Upgrades ({1})'.

strings.where: Top-right button (hotkey R): throws the current carpet away and brings a brand-new dirty one.
strings.note: Short button label.

strings.where: Top-right button that opens the pause menu (Esc).
Big green button that appears when the carpet is clean: give the carpet back to its owner (the client) and get paid. Hotkey H.
strings.note: Short call to action.

strings.where: Big blue button after a hand-over: bring in the next dirty carpet. Hotkey N.
strings.note: Call to action.

strings.where: Caption of the cleanliness meter (0-100 %), top-left card.
strings.note: Adjective (how clean the carpet is), uppercase. Not a verb.

strings.where: Caption of the dryness meter (100 % = completely dry), under CLEAN.
strings.note: Adjective (how dry the carpet is), uppercase. Not a verb.

strings.where: Percent values on the CLEAN / DRY meters and next to the volume slider, e.g. '85%'.
strings.note: Change only the spacing or the order if your language writes percentages differently (French '85 %' with a no-break space, Turkish '%85'); keep it the same as in '{0}% clean'.

strings.where: Small grey text next to the job timer, e.g. 'par 2:43'.
strings.note: 'par' = the target time for this job (as in golf). {0} = a time like 2:43. Keep it very short; the same word appears in '{0} / par {1}'.

strings.where: Small grey text shown instead of the par time when the carpet has no dirt at all.
strings.note: Lowercase in English because it is secondary text; follow your language's normal casing for such a note.

strings.note: Walking movement; short action label.

strings.note: Rotate the view by moving the mouse; short action label.

strings.where: First-person control legend beside a left mouse button icon.
strings.note: Verb: hold the button to operate the cleaning tool. Distinct from the CLEAN percentage caption.

strings.where: First-person control legend beside the number keys 1 through 0.
strings.note: Choose which cleaning tool is held.

strings.where: Tool name (carpet strip and shop). A hand scraper blade that scrapes dried crust and mud off the carpet.
strings.note: Tool names must be short nouns. Use the same tool words in the hints.

strings.where: Tool name. A vacuum cleaner for dry dust and crumbs.
strings.note: Contrast with 'Wet vacuum'.

strings.where: Tool name. A water hose with a spray nozzle: wets the carpet and rinses it.
Tool name. Sprays cleaning foam (carpet shampoo / detergent foam).
Tool name. A rotary scrubbing brush (a floor-scrubber machine with a spinning brush head).
strings.note: A short word for brush is best.

strings.where: Tool name. A rubber squeegee that pushes water off the carpet.
Tool name. A wet vacuum / extractor that sucks up water and foam.
strings.note: Contrast with 'Dry vacuum'.

strings.where: Tool name. A carpet dryer / air mover blowing warm air.
Floor tool name (right strip). Sprays floor detergent on the tiles.
strings.note: A noun naming the tool; it may name the spray bottle or the product.

strings.where: Floor tool name (right strip). A mop for the tiles.
Hint pill at the top centre: the next step the game suggests. Tool: Scraper.
strings.note: Short imperative instruction to the player. Hints must read as advice for the tool named in 'where'.

strings.key: Vacuum up the dust and crumbs
strings.where: Hint. Tool: Dry vacuum.
Hint. Tool: Hose (soak the dried mud with water).
strings.note: 'it' = the carpet.

strings.where: Hint. Tool: Brush (scrub the softened mud loose).
Hint. Tool: Foam sprayer (the cleaning foam).
strings.note: Here 'detergent' means the cleaning foam of the Foam sprayer, not the floor tool 'Detergent'.

strings.key: Scrub the foam into the stains
strings.where: Hint. Tool: Brush.
Hint. Tool: Squeegee.
strings.note: If your language has no verb for squeegee, say 'Push the dirty water off with the squeegee' in few words.

strings.key: Wet-vac the water and foam out
strings.where: Hint. Tool: Wet vacuum.
strings.note: E.g. 'Suck the water and foam out with the wet vacuum' if there is no verb.

strings.where: Hint. Tool: Hose.
Hint. Tool: Dryer.
strings.note: 'it' = the carpet.

strings.where: Hint when the carpet is perfectly clean and dry.
strings.note: Cheerful.

strings.where: Hint when the carpet is done and the Hand over button is showing.
strings.note: 'hand it over' must match the 'Hand over' button.

strings.where: Hint while the finished carpet flies away to its owner.

strings.key: Carpet away - clean the bare tile, or take a new one
strings.where: Hint after the hand-over: the carpet is gone; the player may clean the bare floor tiles, or take the next carpet.
strings.note: The ' - ' is a dash; use your language's normal dash or punctuation.

strings.where: Hint while the next dirty carpet drops in.
strings.note: Use your language's ellipsis convention.

strings.where: Hint for 2 s when the player presses the key of an inspection lamp they do not own yet.
strings.note: {0} = the item name ('Moisture highlight' or 'Dirt highlight'), {1} = the key of the Upgrades button (U). 'Upgrades' must be your translation of the button.

strings.key: {0}: buy it at the upgrade table
strings.where: First-person hint when an unowned inspection lamp is requested.
strings.note: {0} = localized item name. Upgrades are purchased at a physical workbench in the room.

strings.note: Uppercase.

strings.where: Carpet number badge on the pay slip, e.g. '#12' = the 12th carpet delivered.
strings.note: Keep '#{0}' unless your language uses another number sign (e.g. '№{0}').

strings.where: Pay slip title: how dirty the carpet was. This one: it had no dirt at all.
strings.note: The five soil titles form a scale: Already spotless < Light soil < Medium soil < Heavy soil < Filthy.

strings.where: Pay slip title: moderately soiled.
Pay slip title: heavily soiled.

Small detail under 'Base pay' when the carpet had no dirt.
strings.note: Lowercase secondary text in English.

strings.where: Small detail under 'Base pay', e.g. '85% job': the size of the job in percent (100% = a fully soiled carpet).
strings.note: {0} = a number. Keep the % sign right after {0} unless your language puts a space or places it first.

strings.where: Pay slip line: bonus for finishing fast.

strings.where: Pay slip line: bonus for a 100 % clean carpet.

strings.where: Pay slip line: bonus for a 100 % dry carpet.

strings.where: Detail under 'Combo' when it was achieved.

strings.where: Detail under 'Combo' when it was missed: what it takes.

rich_presence._about: Steam friends-list status lines (Tools/Steam/rich_presence_<steam api language>.vdf). %clean% is replaced by Steam with a value like '72%'. Upload in Steamworks > Community > Rich Presence (Docs/STEAM.md 4).
